glossary.definition: A local HTTP add-on (AnkiWeb code 2055492159) that exposes the running desktop Anki app on http://127.0.0.1:8765, answering POST JSON {action, version:6, params, key?} with {result, error}; it is NOT a hosted API, so a cloud app can only reach it via something running on the user's machine [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2].

The consent-based flow in which a user grants an app scoped access, the app receives an authorization code, exchanges it for a short-lived access token plus a refresh token, and calls the API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>; required for Google Calendar/Tasks private-user data, which has no API-key-only access [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3].

The permission string an OAuth request asks for; for Google Calendar write, auth/calendar (broad) or auth/calendar.events (narrower); least privilege means requesting the narrowest scope that satisfies the feature to limit blast radius [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3].

A Base44 environment-variable store holding external credentials (API keys, client secrets) that only Deno backend functions can read; the pattern for Ollama/WAHA/Google keys, never exposed to client code [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6].

Custom TypeScript running on Deno in an isolated environment, the app's egress point for third-party API calls with protected credentials, webhooks, and custom endpoints; can run on schedules or DB events as Automations [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6].

The Google Calendar events.insert field that, with reminders.useDefault=false, sets per-event notifications each as {method: email|popup, minutes: 0-40320}, max 5 overrides per event [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3].

The Tasks API records a task's due as a date only; the time portion of the timestamp is discarded and cannot be read or written via the API, so Tasks cannot carry a timed reminder and Calendar events must be used instead [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3].

A named WhatsApp Web session created by POST /api/sessions moving STOPPED -> STARTING -> SCAN_QR_CODE -> WORKING/FAILED; the login QR is fetched from GET /api/{session}/auth/qr and re-fetched on each SCAN_QR_CODE event [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §4].

WAHA editions: Core is free/open with 1 session and text-type sends; Plus (paid) adds media (images/files/voice/video), multiple sessions per container, and security extras; automating WhatsApp Web carries an inherent account-ban risk [SIGNAL] [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §4].

A caller-supplied de-duplication token attached to a non-idempotent write (addNote, sendText) so a retried request after a timeout does not create a duplicate; the network-boundary extension of sysloops' idempotent-replay rule [METHOD — design synthesis over EXTERNAL_RECON §2/§4/§6].

nodes.definition: Frame the integration problem: everything this KB governs crosses the study app's process boundary to a service the app does not control, and the app's only egress point is a Base44 Deno backend function [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6]. Two structurally different kinds of boundary exist: (a) HOSTED cloud APIs the backend function can call directly over HTTPS (Google Calendar/Tasks, WAHA if self-hosted with a public URL, Ollama Cloud), and (b) LOCALHOST-only services the cloud can never reach directly — AnkiConnect binds 127.0.0.1:8765 on the user's own machine and is not a hosted API, so a cloud app can only reach it via a bridge running on that machine [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2]. Getting this taxonomy wrong (assuming the cloud can POST to localhost) is the single most expensive integration error, so it is fixed first.

included: the hosted-vs-localhost boundary taxonomy
Base44 backend functions as the sole egress point
the cloud-cannot-reach-localhost constraint

pros.claim: Separating hosted from localhost boundaries up front prevents designing a cloud call to a service the cloud can never reach
pros.example: deciding early that AnkiConnect needs a user-machine bridge instead of trying to POST to localhost from a Deno function

cons.claim: The taxonomy is a design abstraction, not a measured property, so an edge case (a user tunnelling localhost to a public URL) can blur it
cons.example: a user exposing AnkiConnect via a reverse tunnel and expecting the cloud path to work without the security caveats

failure_modes: assuming a cloud backend function can POST to a user's localhost:8765
treating every integration as a uniform hosted HTTPS call
acceptance_tests: the frame names the hosted-vs-localhost split, identifies Base44 backend functions as the egress point, and states the cloud-cannot-reach-localhost constraint with the EXTERNAL_RECON §2 citation
revisit_triggers: a new integration is added whose boundary type is unclear
Base44 changes its backend-function egress model
a localhost service gains a hosted variant

base.update_signal: a new boundary type or a Base44 egress change revises the frame

nodes.definition: Fix the wire contract the boundary calls speak: JSON over HTTP with a method, a path, headers (including Authorization), a request body, and a numeric status class (2xx success, 4xx client error incl. 401 auth / 403 forbidden / 429 rate-limited, 5xx server error). AnkiConnect speaks a single-endpoint variant: every action is a POST to http://127.0.0.1:8765 with body {action, version:6, params, key?} returning {result, error} where a non-null error signals failure [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2]. Google Calendar and WAHA speak conventional resource-path REST (events.insert, POST /api/sendText) [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3/§4]. HTTP verb semantics drive retry safety: GET/PUT/DELETE are idempotent, POST is not, which is why POST writes need de-duplication before any retry.

included: JSON-over-HTTP methods/status/headers
AnkiConnect's single-endpoint {action,version,params}->{result,error} shape
idempotent-vs-non-idempotent verb semantics

pros.claim: A shared wire model lets one client abstraction handle Anki, Google, and WAHA despite their surface differences
pros.example: reading a non-2xx status or a non-null AnkiConnect error field through one error-handling path

cons.claim: AnkiConnect's error-in-body convention breaks the assumption that HTTP status alone signals failure, so a naive client misses errors
cons.example: treating a 200 response from AnkiConnect as success while its error field is non-null

failure_modes: reading only HTTP status and ignoring AnkiConnect's error field
retrying a non-idempotent POST as if it were safe
acceptance_tests: the model states JSON-over-HTTP with status classes, gives AnkiConnect's {action,version:6,params,key?}->{result,error} shape, and distinguishes idempotent GET/PUT/DELETE from non-idempotent POST

base.update_signal: a vendor envelope change or a non-REST integration revises the contract model

nodes.definition: Set the secrets discipline: external credentials (API keys, OAuth client secrets, refresh tokens) live only as per-app Base44 Secrets readable inside Deno backend functions, and are transmitted server-side as request headers, never embedded in client code or committed to the repo [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6]. Concretely: Ollama Cloud is called with header Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY where the key is created at ollama.com/settings/keys and stored as a Secret [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §1]; AnkiConnect's optional apiKey is passed as key in each request body [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2]; WAHA's Api Key authenticates its API calls [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §4]. External services do not let Base44 read your credentials automatically — the user pastes them into Secrets [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6]. A leaked static key is only revocable in the vendor's settings, so keys must never reach the browser.

nodes.definition: Decide, per integration, whether a static credential suffices or a full OAuth 2.0 consent flow is required. Static-key services here: Ollama Cloud (Bearer API key), AnkiConnect (optional apiKey), WAHA (Api Key) — all authenticate with a secret the user pastes once [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §1/§2/§4]. The decision drives the whole integration shape: a static key is a Secret plus a header, while OAuth needs a consent screen, a code exchange, token storage, and refresh. Base44 offers OAuth connectors (Google Workspace) as a distinct integration level for exactly this case [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6].

nodes.definition: Give the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow that gets Google API access for the single user: the app redirects the user to Google's consent screen for the requested scopes; on approval Google returns an authorization CODE to the app's redirect URI; the backend exchanges that code (with the client secret, held as a Secret) for an ACCESS token (short-lived, sent as Authorization: Bearer on each API call) plus a REFRESH token (long-lived, stored to mint new access tokens) [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3 states user-data access requires OAuth 2.0; the code->token->refresh mechanics are FACT of the standard flow, ESTIMATE-to-source-verify against Google's auth page which was egress-blocked in recon]. This is why Google is a connector/OAuth integration, not a pasted secret, and why the app must persist and protect the refresh token like any other credential.

nodes.definition: Choose the narrowest OAuth scope that satisfies each feature. For Google Calendar writes the recon documents the broad write scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar and the narrower https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3]; creating study reminders needs only event read/write, so request calendar.events rather than the full-calendar scope. Least privilege limits the blast radius of a token leak and reduces the consent-screen friction that makes users decline. Scopes are requested at consent time (per the auth-code flow) and are fixed for the life of the grant, so under-scoping forces a re-consent and over-scoping is a standing liability — the scope decision is made before the consent screen is built. [ESTIMATE for the least-privilege recommendation; the scope strings themselves are FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §3.]

excluded: the Tasks scope (folded into the no-Reminders-API node)

nodes.definition: Manage the access-token lifecycle so Google calls do not fail on expiry. The access token from the code exchange is short-lived; when it expires the backend uses the stored refresh token to obtain a new access token without re-prompting the user [FACT of the standard OAuth cycle; ESTIMATE-to-source-verify against Google's live token endpoint, egress-blocked in recon]. Practically: detect a 401 (or pre-empt on known expiry), refresh once, retry the call; if the refresh itself fails (revoked/expired grant) fall back to re-consent, never to a silent broken state. Refresh tokens are the highest-value credential the app holds and are stored as protected Secrets like any static key. This cycle is what makes the once-consented Google integration keep working unattended for the single user.

pros.claim: A refresh-then-retry cycle keeps the integration alive across access-token expiry without user interruption
pros.example: a nightly Calendar write that transparently refreshes an expired token and succeeds

cons.claim: A revoked or expired refresh token silently breaks the integration unless the re-consent fallback is built
cons.example: the user revoking access in their Google account and the app looping on failed refreshes with no re-consent path

failure_modes: treating an expired access token as a hard failure instead of refreshing

acceptance_tests: the node distinguishes short-lived access from long-lived refresh tokens, prescribes refresh-then-retry on expiry and re-consent on refresh failure, tagging the mechanics ESTIMATE-to-source-verify against EXTERNAL_RECON §3

nodes.definition: Make cross-boundary writes safe to retry, extending sysloops' idempotent-replay rule across the network. A timed-out POST may have succeeded server-side, so blindly retrying a non-idempotent write duplicates it: addNote can create a duplicate card, sendText can send a duplicate WhatsApp message [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2/§4 for the actions; the duplication risk is a standard-distributed-systems FACT]. Mitigations: prefer the vendor's own de-duplication where it exists (AnkiConnect's canAddNotes / options.allowDuplicate + duplicateScope let the caller check before adding [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §2]); otherwise attach a caller-side idempotency key / natural-key check so a retry is a no-op. Retries use bounded exponential backoff with a cap and a dead-letter for permanent failures, never an unbounded hammer loop. [ESTIMATE — design synthesis grounded in the cited actions.]

vendor de-dup (canAddNotes/allowDuplicate) and caller-side idempotency keys
bounded exponential backoff with a dead-letter

pros.claim: De-duplicating before retry lets the app recover from timeouts without creating duplicate cards or messages
pros.example: using canAddNotes to skip an addNote whose card already exists after a timed-out first attempt

cons.claim: Not every vendor exposes a de-dup primitive, so some idempotency must be reconstructed from natural keys that can be imperfect
cons.example: inferring a WhatsApp message was already sent from app-side state because WAHA offers no message idempotency key

failure_modes: retrying addNote/sendText without de-duplication and creating duplicates

acceptance_tests: the node states the duplicate-write risk on retried POSTs, prescribes vendor de-dup (canAddNotes/allowDuplicate) or caller-side idempotency keys, and requires bounded exponential backoff with a dead-letter, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §2/§4

nodes.definition: Respect vendor rate limits and transient-error signals rather than hammering. A 429 (Too Many Requests) or a vendor-specific limit response means back off — honour any Retry-After, otherwise apply exponential backoff with jitter and a ceiling [standard-HTTP FACT]. Recon-specific limits: Ollama Cloud's exact rate limits/pricing tiers are UNKNOWN (not in reachable docs) and must be discovered, not assumed [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §1]; WAHA/WhatsApp-Web automation is ban-sensitive so message pacing is a safety concern, not just a throughput one [SIGNAL, FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §4]; Google enforces per-project quotas [ESTIMATE — standard for Google APIs, to source-verify]. Backoff composes with the idempotency rule: a retried call after a 429 must still be de-duplicated. Sending too fast to WhatsApp is itself a driver of ban risk, so pacing is doubly load-bearing there.

nodes.definition: Handle inbound events where a vendor calls the app instead of the reverse. Base44 backend functions can serve custom endpoints and webhooks [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6], and WAHA emits session events (e.g. session.status transitioning to SCAN_QR_CODE, prompting a QR re-fetch) [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §4]. A safe webhook receiver: (a) authenticates the caller (shared secret/signature) so arbitrary internet traffic cannot drive app state; (b) responds fast and processes asynchronously so a slow handler does not cause vendor retries; (c) treats delivery as at-least-once and therefore de-duplicates, reusing the idempotency rule since the same event may arrive twice. Webhooks only work for hosted/self-hosted services with a reachable callback URL — a localhost AnkiConnect cannot receive them, reinforcing the boundary taxonomy. [ESTIMATE — synthesis over EXTERNAL_RECON §4/§6.]

nodes.definition: Establish Base44 backend functions as the concrete egress mechanism. They run custom TypeScript on Deno in an isolated environment and exist precisely for business logic, third-party API calls with protected credentials, webhooks, and custom endpoints [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6]. Every outbound integration in this KB (Google, WAHA, Ollama, and the cloud-side of the Anki bridge) is implemented as or behind a backend function, because that is the only place a per-app Secret can be read and a server-side HTTPS call can be made. nodes.definition: Pin the AnkiConnect access architecture. conflict_axes.name: timed_reminder_vs_no_reminders_api
conflict_axes.description: The app wants timed reminders, but there is no Google Reminders API and Tasks due is date-only, so the timed path is constrained to Calendar events.
poles: use lightweight Tasks for reminders
use Calendar events for timed reminders
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route anything needing a clock time to Calendar events.insert with overrides; use Tasks only for date-only to-dos

conflict_axes.name: retry_for_reliability_vs_duplicate_writes
conflict_axes.description: Retrying a timed-out write improves reliability but a non-idempotent POST may have already succeeded, creating duplicates.
poles: retry aggressively for reliability
de-duplicate before every retry
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: attach vendor de-dup (canAddNotes/allowDuplicate) or an idempotency key so retries are no-ops on already-applied writes

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_rate_limit_and_ban_safety
conflict_axes.description: Sending faster improves responsiveness but trips vendor rate limits and, for WhatsApp, raises ban risk.
poles: send at full speed
pace and back off within limits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honour 429/Retry-After with jittered backoff and pace WhatsApp sends, treating pacing as a safety control

conflict_axes.name: waha_reach_vs_account_ban_risk
conflict_axes.description: WAHA gives real WhatsApp reach but is an unofficial client with an inherent account-ban risk.
poles: make WAHA a supported reminder channel
keep WAHA optional and off by default
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep WAHA optional/off-by-default, text-only on Core, so its value is available without a hard dependency on a ban-prone channel

conflict_axes.name: app_control_vs_ankiconnect_fsrs_gap
conflict_axes.description: The app wants full programmatic scheduling control, but AnkiConnect exposes no FSRS action so retention tuning stays in Anki's UI.
poles: drive all scheduling through the API
set FSRS/retention in Anki's UI and use API for workload only
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use perDay limits + setDueDate/forgetCards via the API and defer FSRS/desired-retention to Anki's UI; never invent an FSRS action

conflict_axes.name: connector_reuse_vs_raw_call_control
conflict_axes.description: A Base44 OAuth connector reuses built machinery but may not exist or fit; a raw backend-function call gives control but re-implements auth.
poles: use a prebuilt connector
hand-roll a raw Secret-based call
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer the connector where it exists (Google Workspace) and fall back to a raw call only when no connector fits

conflict_axes.name: verify_now_vs_defer_unknown_to_method
conflict_axes.description: Some vendor facts (Ollama limits, WAHA prices, live Google field names) are UNKNOWN in recon, tempting an assumed value versus a deferral.
poles: assume a plausible value to ship now
carry the UNKNOWN with a [METHOD] to obtain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never hard-code an UNKNOWN limit or field; carry it as a named [METHOD] and verify against live docs before relying on it

edge_cases.description: A cloud backend function is written to POST directly to the user's localhost:8765
edge_cases.trigger: AnkiConnect is treated as a hosted API reachable from the cloud
edge_cases.mitigation: relay AnkiConnect through a user-machine bridge and keep the cloud function on the hosted side only

edge_cases.description: A retried addNote or sendText after a timeout creates a duplicate card or message
edge_cases.trigger: a non-idempotent POST is retried without de-duplication
edge_cases.mitigation: use canAddNotes/allowDuplicate or a caller-side idempotency key so a retry is a no-op

edge_cases.description: An API key or refresh token is embedded in client-side code or committed to the repo
edge_cases.trigger: a credential is placed outside a backend-only Secret
edge_cases.mitigation: keep all credentials in per-app Secrets read only in backend functions, revoke and rotate any that leaked

edge_cases.description: The app expects a Google Reminders API or a timed Google Tasks due
edge_cases.trigger: reminder design assumes an API that does not exist or a Tasks time that is discarded
edge_cases.mitigation: route timed reminders through Calendar events.insert with overrides and use Tasks for date-only to-dos

edge_cases.description: An FSRS action is assumed on AnkiConnect and retention is 'set' via the API
edge_cases.trigger: the app tries to drive FSRS/desired-retention through AnkiConnect
edge_cases.mitigation: tune workload via perDay + setDueDate/forgetCards and set FSRS/retention in Anki's UI; never invent an FSRS action

edge_cases.description: A Google access token expires mid-job and the call fails hard
edge_cases.trigger: expiry is treated as a permanent failure instead of triggering a refresh
edge_cases.mitigation: refresh once on 401/known expiry and retry; fall back to re-consent only if the refresh token itself is invalid

edge_cases.description: A WAHA session drops to SCAN_QR_CODE and the reminder channel silently stalls
edge_cases.trigger: the QR is not re-fetched on the new SCAN_QR_CODE event
edge_cases.mitigation: watch session.status and re-fetch the QR on each SCAN_QR_CODE, surfacing a re-scan prompt rather than failing quietly

edge_cases.description: WhatsApp messages are bursted fast enough to trip ban heuristics
edge_cases.trigger: sends are not paced and the account is flagged as automated
edge_cases.mitigation: pace sends, keep WAHA optional/off-by-default, and treat pacing as a ban-safety control

edge_cases.description: An unauthenticated webhook endpoint lets arbitrary callers spoof vendor events
edge_cases.trigger: a Base44 endpoint accepts webhook calls without verifying the caller
edge_cases.mitigation: authenticate every webhook with a shared secret/signature and de-duplicate at-least-once deliveries

edge_cases.description: A scheduled Automation reruns after a crash and double-writes to a vendor
edge_cases.trigger: a recurring cross-boundary job is not idempotent
edge_cases.mitigation: make the Automation idempotent with de-dup so a rerun yields no duplicate cards, events, or messages

edge_cases.description: An UNKNOWN vendor limit (Ollama rate limit, WAHA price) is hard-coded as an assumed value
edge_cases.trigger: a plausible number is baked in instead of being verified
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the UNKNOWN as a named [METHOD] to obtain and verify against live docs before relying on it

edge_cases.description: A browser call to AnkiConnect fails because the app origin is not allowlisted
edge_cases.trigger: the app's web origin is missing from webCorsOriginList and the permission popup is unhandled
edge_cases.mitigation: add the app origin to webCorsOriginList and guide the user through the one-time in-Anki permission approval

dominance_rules.rule: The user-machine local bridge dominates any direct cloud call to AnkiConnect
dominance_rules.rationale: AnkiConnect binds localhost on the user's machine and is not hosted, so the cloud cannot reach it directly
dominance_rules.trigger: an Anki call is about to be made from a cloud backend function
dominance_rules.action: route it through a user-machine bridge and never POST to localhost from the cloud

dominance_rules.rule: OAuth consent dominates a pasted static key for private Google data
dominance_rules.rationale: Google has no API-key-only access for private calendars
dominance_rules.trigger: a Google Calendar/Tasks integration is being authorized
dominance_rules.action: use an OAuth connector/flow with a refresh token, not a pasted secret

dominance_rules.rule: Calendar events dominate Tasks for any timed reminder
dominance_rules.rationale: there is no Reminders API and Tasks due is date-only with the time discarded
dominance_rules.trigger: a reminder needs a clock time
dominance_rules.action: create a Calendar event with reminder overrides and reserve Tasks for date-only to-dos

dominance_rules.rule: De-duplication dominates a bare retry for non-idempotent writes
dominance_rules.rationale: a timed-out POST may have already succeeded, so a blind retry duplicates it
dominance_rules.trigger: addNote or sendText is retried after a timeout
dominance_rules.action: attach vendor de-dup or an idempotency key so the retry is a no-op

dominance_rules.rule: Anki's UI dominates the API for FSRS/desired-retention settings
dominance_rules.trigger: the app wants to change FSRS or desired retention
dominance_rules.action: tune workload via perDay + setDueDate/forgetCards over the API and set FSRS/retention in Anki's UI

dominance_rules.rule: Least-privilege scope dominates the broad scope
dominance_rules.rationale: a narrow scope limits the blast radius of a leaked token
dominance_rules.trigger: an OAuth scope is being requested
dominance_rules.action: request calendar.events rather than the full calendar scope unless a feature truly needs more

dominance_rules.rule: A named [METHOD]-to-obtain dominates a hard-coded UNKNOWN value
dominance_rules.rationale: assuming an unverified limit or field ships a fabricated fact
dominance_rules.trigger: an Ollama limit, WAHA price, or live Google field is needed but UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.action: carry it as a [METHOD] and verify against live docs before relying on it

dominance_rules.rule: Idempotent Automations dominate best-effort scheduled jobs
dominance_rules.rationale: a non-idempotent recurring push double-writes on rerun after a crash
dominance_rules.trigger: a recurring cross-boundary job writes to a vendor
dominance_rules.action: make the Automation idempotent with de-dup so a rerun yields no duplicates

dominance_rules.rule: An authenticated webhook dominates an open endpoint
dominance_rules.rationale: an unauthenticated endpoint lets arbitrary callers spoof app state
dominance_rules.trigger: a Base44 endpoint receives vendor webhooks
dominance_rules.action: verify a shared secret/signature and de-duplicate at-least-once deliveries

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify each integration hosted-vs-localhost before designing its call path
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a cloud call to a localhost-only service and re-architecting to a bridge later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide static-key vs OAuth before wiring any auth
anti_rework_rules.prevents: coding a pasted-key path for Google that private calendars reject and reworking to OAuth

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm AnkiConnect exposes no FSRS action before promising programmatic retention control
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing an FSRS-over-API feature that cannot exist and ripping it out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route timed reminders to Calendar from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building on a phantom Reminders API or a date-only Tasks due and redoing the reminder layer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add idempotency keys/de-dup when the first non-idempotent write is wired
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a history of duplicate cards or messages from retried POSTs that must be cleaned up

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep credentials in backend-only Secrets from the first integration
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a leaked key in client code or the repo forcing revocation, rotation, and rebuild

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make WAHA optional and off by default before depending on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a ban-killed WhatsApp channel taking down a feature that was made to require it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry every recon UNKNOWN as a [METHOD] rather than an assumed constant
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hard-coding a wrong limit or field and reworking when live docs contradict it

priority_rationale: The boundary frame and REST/secrets discipline come first because they decide, for every integration, where the call runs and how its credential is held; the API-key-vs-OAuth decision and the OAuth code/scope/refresh nodes then build the authorization spine that Google needs; the reliability nodes (idempotency, backoff, webhooks) and the Base44 platform nodes (backend functions, integration levels, Automations) supply the runtime the calls execute in; the concrete vendor contracts (AnkiConnect local bridge + note/scheduling/security, Google Calendar events + no-Reminders-API, WAHA session/QR + sendText/limits) instantiate the frame against real endpoints from EXTERNAL_RECON; and the boundary-contract verdict comes last because it composes every upstream decision into a go/optional/no-go stack whose each contract has a defined auth mode, idempotency, and degraded behaviour.
